transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-07
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel (Adeptis Head of MLOps), Liam O'Connor (VP Eng), Sven Meyer (SRE), Aisha Khan (Procurement)

Summary: quick renewal check-in, scope capacity uplift for EU + APAC regions, discuss contract extension timing and pilot benchmarks for 8k-token LLM calls. Action items captured and next steps agreed.

Topics: renewal timing; committed capacity tiers; regional activation (Ireland, Frankfurt, Tokyo); VPC/KMS and compliance; latency SLOs; dedicated vs hosted routing; benchmarking plan.

00:00:06 - Sofia Martinez: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um we'll do a short run through — our goal is to confirm the commit tier you're leaning to, the region sequence and any legal / security blockers for renewal.
00:00:18 - Maya Patel: yep thanks sofia, appreciate it. quick note, we've got liam and sven on here because they're owning the infra side, and aisha for procurement. we ran the usage report last week, so we can look at numbers.
00:00:32 - Liam O'Connor: hi all. main ask — can we get predictable throughput for peak times in europe and japan? previously we saw 2x spikes that degraded p99.
00:00:45 - Daniel Cho: right, and that's where dedicated pools come in; we can reserve GPU capacity with capacity headroom and autoscale policies. for the 2x spikes — we recommend a small burst pool plus prefix/KV caching to reduce token re-computation.
00:00:58 - Sven Meyer: when you say KV cahce — kv cache — is that sticky per session? like if we pin convo IDs, will each worker have warm cache or do we need external cache?
00:01:12 - Daniel Cho: good question. runtime uses in-host KV cache for active sessions — that reduces latency for repeated prefixes; for cross-instance sharing we suggest prefix caching at the routing layer or a lightweight external cache. there's some lossiness tradeoffs though.
00:01:28 - Maya Patel: got it. on regions — our legal team wants EU first (Ireland), then Frankfurt, then Tokyo. is there a recommended order for activation? any big lead times?
00:01:41 - Priya Rao: typically Ireland is the quickest, Frankfurt needs a short validation for network routing and private link, and Tokyo tends to be the longest due to capacity provisioning windows; we can stage them — Ireland + dedicated reserve in 2 weeks, Frankfurt in next sprint, Tokyo in 6-8 weeks.
00:01:58 - Aisha Khan: procurement question — if we sign a 12-month commit vs 24-month, how much of a price delta are we looking at? also do we get a pro rata for region additions?
00:02:12 - Sofia Martinez: good Q. rough ballpark: 12-month commit gives X% off list, 24-month adds another Y% and we can include a region add-on credit for first 3 months for each new geo during onboarding. i'll send the updated pricing matrix after this call.
00:02:26 - Maya Patel: can you show the numbers now? even top-level?
00:02:29 - Sofia Martinez: sorry i don't have the spreadsheet open in this tab, but i'll follow up with an email within 48 hours.
00:02:34 - Liam O'Connor: ok, that's fine. more technical — we care about 99th pctl latency under an 8k token tail. our current production prompts average 3.5k but some inference paths spike to 8k with context.
00:02:47 - Daniel Cho: understood. for that pattern we recommend quantized model variants plus tuned batching. the tradeoff is slightly higher median latency if you over-batch, so we'll tune batch size to meet p99 SLO. we'll run a bench with your exact prompt mix.
00:03:03 - Sven Meyer: also what about failover? if ireland has an outage, do we automagically route to frankfurt? what about data sovereignty?
00:03:14 - Priya Rao: routing policies are configurable — you can set region failover but we can restrict fallbacks for data-sovereign routes. if you require EU-residency, we can keep requests in-region and use dedicated failover to other EU zones only.
00:03:29 - Maya Patel: that's critical. legal won't let us have EU data leave the region even for failover unless it's to certified EU sites.
00:03:36 - Sofia Martinez: noted. we'll set a policy that forbids cross-region spill to non-EU for those keys. we'll document the routing policy and include it in the SOW.
00:03:44 - Aisha Khan: procurement: can you confirm audit logs retention and whether those counts towards usage?
00:03:51 - Priya Rao: audit logs are kept per contract; retention tiers are separate add-ons and don't count toward token usage. we can provide syslog or S3 export for your SIEM.
00:04:02 - Liam O'Connor: on private connectivity — we want VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. any gaps?
00:04:09 - Daniel Cho: we support VPC private endpoints, customer KMS integrations and HSM options for enterprise tiers. there are a few steps: network validation, cert exchange, and KMS key policy review — typically a 1-2 week integration if access is ready.
00:04:23 - Sven Meyer: does KMS integration add latency? for token signing or embedding storage?
00:04:29 - Priya Rao: minimal — KMS ops are async for most flows; there's a short crypto handshake but runtime caches keys. we'll include the expected overhead in the integration doc.
00:04:40 - Maya Patel: can we run a pilot with a small commit: like 250k tokens/day reserved, plus burst up to 1M? we want to validate cost and p99 before scaling.
00:04:51 - Sofia Martinez: yes, a pilot is a great next step. typical pilot is 60 days with a committed baseline and burst pool. we'll propose two pilot tiers in the follow-up (Pilot A: 250k/day baseline + 1M burst, Pilot B: 500k/day baseline + 2M burst).
00:05:07 - Aisha Khan: and how does billing look during pilot? monthly invoicing or upfront?
00:05:11 - Sofia Martinez: standard is monthly invoicing with consumption reconciliation against the commit. if you prefer prepay on pilot, we can accommodate.
00:05:19 - Liam O'Connor: latency SLOs — do you offer financial credits for p99 breaches?
00:05:24 - Priya Rao: for dedicated contracts we do include SLOs and escalation playbooks — credits are available for sustained breaches per SLO clause. for pilots we typically offer operational support SLAs but not full financial credits; can discuss for enterprise commit.
00:05:38 - Daniel Cho: i'll add that we'll run an end-to-end bench where we replay their traffic (anonymized) against our routing and kernel selection. we can measure p50/p95/p99 and tail variance.
00:05:49 - Maya Patel: great. do you support multiple model variants in the same routing policy — like a quantized fallback if the primary is slow?
00:05:56 - Daniel Cho: yes, model variants and automatic fallback is supported; policy can be latency-first or cost-first. it's automated: if primary exceeds threshold we'll failover to a compatible quantized variant.
00:06:08 - Sven Meyer: small nit — we need to validate that the quantized variant preserves quality for our NLU tasks. do you do evals?
00:06:14 - Daniel Cho: yep, we can run head-to-head evals on your prompt set — quality regressions flagged and tied back to the rollout. we'll provide a short report for each candidate variant.
00:06:26 - Aisha Khan: procurement: is there a minimum notice for region deprovisioning or scale-down?
00:06:32 - Sofia Martinez: for committed capacity, 30 days notice for changes to tier; for region deprovisioning we align with contract terms — usually 60-90 days to coordinate resource teardown.
00:06:44 - Liam O'Connor: outstanding item — egress costs. do you have a typical number for EU -> US egress if fallbacks happen?
00:06:51 - Priya Rao: egress depends on cloud provider; we can estimate but will include region-specific egress estimates in the pricing sheet. also we can limit fallbacks to avoid cross-border egress.
00:07:04 - Maya Patel: ok. can we review the pilot acceptance criteria? what metrics do we need to pass to approve full commit?
00:07:11 - Daniel Cho: propose: sustained p99 under X ms for peak hour load, error rate under 0.1%, throughput meeting committed qps for 2 consecutive weeks, and no model-quality degradation above threshold on the eval set.
00:07:25 - Maya Patel: that's reasonable, send it in writing.
00:07:28 - Sofia Martinez: will do.
00:07:31 - Aisha Khan: timeline — if we sign this month, when can we start pilot?
00:07:35 - Sofia Martinez: if contracts and PO are in by July 15, we can kick pilot in July 22 with Ireland activation first.
00:07:42 - Liam O'Connor: final question — do you integrate with our observability stack? we want token-level tracing to our datadog and jaeger traces.
00:07:49 - Daniel Cho: yes, we have tracing hooks and can stream token-level events to datadog or open-telemetry collectors; we'll share the integration guide.
00:07:58 - Maya Patel: perfect.
00:08:00 - Sofia Martinez: recap - action items: i'll send pricing and region credit examples, daniel runs the bench and priya shares SOC2/KMS docs. maya to confirm prompt set and traffic profile. we'll aim to have follow-up by next thursday. anything else?
00:08:14 - Liam O'Connor: no, that's it. thanks.
00:08:16 - Maya Patel: thanks folks, appreciate the clear plan.
00:08:19 - Sofia Martinez: thanks everyone, talk soon.
